summary: FastAPI [GAP: API and worker telemetry] -> send_task [GAP: Order enqueue outcomes] -> Redis -> fulfill_order [GAP: Fulfillment outcomes and delay]

evidence.finding: FastAPI, Celery and Redis dependencies without OpenTelemetry setup.
FastAPI sends work to the independent Redis-backed Celery worker.
Routes are listed from application source; this packet covers only the selected work.
Compose starts Redis, API and worker as separate services.

findings.title: API and worker telemetry
findings.gap: The API and independent Celery worker have no OpenTelemetry initialization.
findings.impact: Both processes retain their Compose startup and emit baseline FastAPI, Celery and Redis telemetry with distinct configurable identities.
findings.required_fix: Both processes retain their Compose startup and emit baseline FastAPI, Celery and Redis telemetry with distinct configurable identities.
acceptance_criteria: Both processes retain their Compose startup and emit baseline FastAPI, Celery and Redis telemetry with distinct configurable identities.
constraints: Preserve existing application behavior, telemetry owners and supported startup paths; keep private data out of telemetry dimensions.

findings.title: Order enqueue outcomes
findings.gap: The API stores pending state before send_task, whose failure is not measured.
findings.impact: Successful and failed enqueue attempts have bounded, accurate outcome telemetry.

findings.title: Fulfillment outcomes and delay
findings.gap: Fulfillment completes asynchronously without app-owned outcome or timing signals.
findings.impact: Task success/failure and an accurately measured delay, age or duration reveal failed or slow work; broker fleet state is not inferred from local state.
